'''Jette Baagøe''' (née Svendsen, born 1946) is the director of the [[Danish Museum of Hunting and Forestry]] in [[Hørsholm]] where she has worked since 1984.<ref name=kvinfo>{{cite web|url=http://www.kvinfo.dk/side/383/action/2/vis/943/|title=Jette Baagøe|publisher=Kvinfo|accessdate=19 July 2015 |language=Danish}}</ref> She headed the steering group that began work on the nomination of [[Par force hunting landscape in North Zealand|The par force hunting landscape in North Zealand]], which was inscribed on the [[UNESCO World Heritage List]] on 4 July 2015.<ref name="Dansk Jagt- og Skovbrugsmuseum">{{cite web|url=http://www.jagtskov.dk/presse/artikel/verdensarv-i-nordsjaelland/|title=Verdensarv i Nordsjælland: 4. juli 2015 optog UNESCOs verdensarvskomité Parforcejagtlandskabet i Nordsjælland på den fornemme liste over verdens kulturarv|publisher=Dansk Jagt- og Skovbrugsmuseum|date=7 July 2015|access-date=19 July 2015|language=Danish|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722123202/http://www.jagtskov.dk/presse/artikel/verdensarv-i-nordsjaelland/|archive-date=22 July 2015|df=}}</ref>

==Biography==
Baagøe studied at the [[University of Copenhagen]], graduating in botany, zoology, geology and geography in 1973 with a PhD in botany in 1976. In addition to her museum work, she headed the now defunct Federikborg Cultural Environment Council and has served as a member of the Danish branch of the [[International Council for Game and Wildlife Conservation (CIC)]]. She has written and lectured on [[par force hunting]] in Denmark, on the [[Jægersborg Dyrehave]] and on how forests were depicted during the [[Golden Age of Danish Painting]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kulturarv.dk/1001fortaellinger/da_DK/profile/jette-baagoee|title=Jette Baagøe|publisher=Kulturarv|accessdate=19 July 2015 |language=Danish}}</ref>

As director, she hopes to modernize the Danish Museum of Hunting and Forestry and simplify its name. She believes it should have a broader mandate covering man's relationship with nature. She is especially interested in the unique network of forest roads in the area which were used for par force hunting by the Danish kings in the 17th and 18th centuries and now expects the museum will benefit from the recent UNESCO heritage listing.<ref name="Dansk Jagt- og Skovbrugsmuseum"/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.b.dk/kultur/i-skovens-dybe-stille-ro|title=I skovens dybe stille ro|newspaper=Berlingske|author=Bent Blüdnikow|date=25 January 2015|accessdate=19 July 2015 |language=Danish}}</ref> Although the listing is under cultural heritage rather than nature, Baagøe hopes it will result in full protection of the forests themselves.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sn.dk/Nordsjaelland/Jagtstier-i-verdensarv-oploeb/artikel/486727|title=Jagtstier i verdensarv-opløb |publisher=SN.dk|accessdate=19 July 2015 |language=Danish|date=2015-05-08 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jette Baagøe was born and raised in [[Ringsted]] and now lives in [[Lyngby]]. She is married to Ib Welling and together they have one child Snorre Welling.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoersholm.lokalavisen.dk/jaegeren-er-byttet-i-historiens-brogede-billedbog-/20070804/artikler/708040324|title=Jægeren er byttet i historiens brogede billedbog|publisher=Hørsholm Localavisen|accessdate=19 July 2015|language=Danish|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084752/http://hoersholm.lokalavisen.dk/jaegeren-er-byttet-i-historiens-brogede-billedbog-/20070804/artikler/708040324|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards==
Baagøe has received several awards for her work including the [[Order of the Dannebrog]] in 1998.<ref name=kvinfo/>
